name: cortex-ide
description: IDE professionnel Electron avec orchestration d'agents IA multi-providers
author: Cortex IDE Team
//trustedDependencies: better-sqlite3 ships a native addon. Bun skips postinstall scripts unless the package is trusted, which leaves no compiled binary — or a binary built for a different NODE_MODULE_VERSION. Vitest runs the suite under plain Node, so an unbuilt/stale addon fails every database test at `new Database()`. Keep this list in sync with any native dependency.

scripts.//paper: The Paper file `IDE New 01` owns the design. These commands pull from it; nothing under packages/tokens/src/*.generated.* or design/paper/ is hand-written. Needs PAPER_MCP_URL, PAPER_MCP_AUTH and PAPER_FILE_ID.
scripts.//visual: Renders every routed screen at its artboard's exact viewport and writes the captures beside the Paper references. Reporting rather than pass/fail: Paper only returns JPEG, so a strict comparison would fail on compression artefacts. Exact-value checking lives in packages/ui's fidelity suite.
scripts.//paper:diff: Pixel-compares the captures against the Paper references. The references are JPEG, so a perfect implementation cannot reach 0% - the numbers are for tracking movement, not for gating.
scripts.//test: Vitest is the only unit-test runner. The root config delegates to every packages/*/vitest.config.ts plus tests/vitest.config.ts, so `test` runs the whole suite and `test:discovery` proves no file on disk was left unclaimed. Playwright owns tests/e2e, tests/visual and tests/accessibility via test:e2e.
scripts.//test:unit: Negated rather than an explicit project list: a new package would silently drop out of an allowlist, which is the same silent-skip failure the discovery guard exists to prevent.
scripts.//test:performance:budgets: The benches must run in the SAME invocation that scores them: check-budgets.ts reads tests/performance/results/, refuses files older than an hour, and fails when a budget has no measurement. Running the checker alone would score whatever is on disk. The results dir is cleared first so a deleted benchmark shows up as a missing metric instead of leaving its last good result behind.
scripts.test:performance:budgets: rm -rf tests/performance/results && bun run test:performance && bun tests/performance/check-budgets.ts --max-age-seconds=600
scripts.test:all: bun run test:coverage && bun run test:e2e
